question.text: A potentiometer wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math> is connected in series with a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>25</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> battery and an external resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>30</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Ω</mi></math>. A cell of emf <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math> in secondary circuit is balanced by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>250</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> long potentiometer wire. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>E</mi></math> (in volt) is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>x</mi><mn>10</mn></mfrac></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is _____ .

solution.text:
Since the given resistance is in series, so, total resistance R=20+30=50 Ω

Given,

Potential difference=25 V

Current I=VR=2550=0.5 A

Also, Potential gradient =VpdL=IRL

Where, Vpd=potential drop at wire

L=Length of wire

Potential gradient=20×0.510=1 V m-1

So, Emf of the cell is

E=Potential gradient×Balancing Length

E= 1× 250100

E= 2.5 V=2510 V

Thus, x=25.
